offence_severity: Life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000 each; in default, further simple imprisonment for a period of3 months
physical_harm: Injuries caused by sharp-edged weapon and blunt object like lathi resulting in death
motive: Alleged motive was that deceased had an evil eye on the women-folk of the family of the accused
key_evidence_accepted: The ocular version that the accused persons had inflicted the injuries with weapons due to which the victim died was corroborated by medical evidence. The doctor clearly stated that injury Nos. I to 10 were caused by sharp-edged weapon and the contusion in the form of a lathi mark on the back, right side and multiple bruises and contusions in the form of lathi marks on the front chest and both arms were caused by blunt object like lathi.
witness_credibility: The version of the complainant, Anand Singh-PW5, being the father of the deceased, was found to be quite reliable. He would be the last person to spare the actual assailant and would not implicate the accused falsely. He had no enmity with the accused persons.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 4.7.2003; Trial judgment: 06.08.2009; High Court decision: 06.08.2009; Supreme Court decision: 25.02.2016
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Pushpinder Singh, Kumar Km1ikay, Aruneshwar Gupta, Ama1j it Singh Bedi; Counsel for the State: S.U.K. Sagar, Vishwa Pal Singh, Ms. Naresh Bakshi, Rao Ranjit
investigation_status: FIR registered on 5.7.2003; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction recorded; High Court: Acquitted Sandeep, convicted remaining 5 accused; Supreme Court: Affirmed conviction and sentence
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased, Partap, was mercilessly beaten and murdered by the accused appellants using weapons like lathis and swords, leading to his death. The version of the complainant, Anand Singh, was found reliable and corroborated by medical evidence. The FIR delay was satisfactorily explained as Anand Singh became unwell after his son's death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused were falsely implicated in the case, as Partap had tried to outrage the modesty of Monika and was beaten by villagers. The FIR was delayed, and the prosecution failed to examine certain witnesses, which the defence claimed undermined the case against the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the version of an eye-witness, particularly a father of the deceased, is reliable if there is no motive to falsely implicate the accused and if the statement is corroborated by medical evidence.
precedent_relied_upon: The State of U.P. & Anr. v. Jaggo alias Jagdish & Ors. (AIR 1971 SC 1586); Bahal Singh v. State of Haryana (AIR 1976 SC 2032)
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the courts found the accused guilty of causing the death of Partap through violent means, and the conviction was deemed correct and justified based on the evidence and witness statements.
other_sentence_order: The accused were sentenced to life imprisonment and fined Rs.5,000 each, with additional imprisonment for default. The High Court acquitted Sandeep as his name was not mentioned in the FIR.
